justification: Both surfaces show a single animal figure rendered in low relief on the broad face of an upright rectangular stone pillar, with the creature's body in profile and limbs schematically indicated, and in A a hand-like motif appears below, suggesting an anthropomorphic pillar. The strongest difference is the specific subject and posture: A shows a small vertically descending creature (limbs splayed against the shaft) above a hand, whereas B shows a large horizontally striding quadruped, likely a predator, dominating the panel with no accompanying hand or body-part motif.
